title: Missouri: history overview
d: Missouri: the Show-Me State, admitted 1821 (24th); capital Jefferson City.
definition: Missouri: the Show-Me State, admitted 1821 (24th); capital Jefferson City.
description: Missouri — "Show-Me State" — entered the Union 1821 (24th). Its capital is Jefferson City and its largest city is Kansas City. Osage; Lewis & Clark; gateway west. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Missouri achieved statehood 1821 (24th). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Civil War border state. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Missouri its number among the states.

title: The statehood story
d: How Missouri went from territory to state.
definition: How Missouri went from territory to state.
description: The statehood story of Missouri: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Railroads; beer; BBQ. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Missouri's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Jefferson City
d: Jefferson City is the capital of Missouri.
definition: Jefferson City is the capital of Missouri.
description: Jefferson City has been the seat of Missouri government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Missouri's largest is Kansas City — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Show-Me State
description: The nickname "Show-Me State" captures how Missouri sees itself — and how America sees it. The Gateway Arch rose in 1965 as the westward monument. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Salus populi suprema lex esto (The welfare of the people shall be the supreme law)."
